name: barbrabell
description: Plan, log and track strength training: today's workout, logging sets, body weight and sleep, progress toward lift and race goals, and swaps for exercises that hurt. Coaches use it to write and review their clients' training.

interface.longDescription:
Barbrabell plans, logs and tracks strength training. It holds a person's goals, their multi-week program, each day's planned session and every set they log, and shares them with the Barbrabell iPhone app.

Ask what today's workout is and it shows each exercise with its sets, reps, load and the coach's notes. Say how the session went and it logs it, set by set with RPE. Tell it your weigh-in or how you slept and it saves them. Ask how you're doing and it reports each goal (a lift max, reps in a row, body weight or a race time) against your program's pace, from your own logged sets. If an exercise hurts, it suggests alternatives that fit your equipment, and changes a planned session only when you say yes, with undo.

Strength coaches use the same tools for their clients: see who needs attention this week, write and adjust a client's program from what they logged, and invite new clients to the app.

Who it's for: people following a strength program, and the coaches who write them. It plans and records training; it doesn't give medical advice or diagnose injuries.
defaultPrompt: How am I doing on my goals?
Log my workout: it felt like RPE 8.

positive.expected_behavior: Shows today's planned session from their program: each exercise with sets, reps and load (or the easy run's distance on a run day), and the coach's notes, such as "Reset each rep." on deadlifts.

positive.description: An athlete logs a finished workout.
positive.prompt: I just did today's workout as planned. It felt like RPE 8. Log it.
positive.expected_behavior: Logs today's planned sets with RPE 8 and confirms what was logged in a line or two. On an easy-run day it logs the run with log_run instead. If today is already logged, it asks before replacing it.

positive.description: An athlete logs body weight and sleep.
positive.prompt: Log my weigh-in: 176 lb. I slept 7 hours last night.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves today's weigh-in of 176 lb and 7 hours of sleep, and confirms both.

positive.description: An athlete checks progress toward their goals.
positive.prompt: How am I doing on my goals?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports each goal (back squat 225 lb, bench press 185 lb, 10 pull-ups and a 5K in 26:00, all by 2027-01-30): where it is now from their logged sets, whether they're on pace, and any wins.

positive.description: An athlete asks for an alternative to an exercise that hurts.
positive.prompt: My knee hurts on back squats. What can I do instead?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists alternatives to the back squat that use their equipment, best first, without diagnosing the knee. It may offer to change an upcoming session, and changes nothing unless they say yes.

negative.description: Unrelated request. Barbrabell holds strength training, not weather, so none of its tools should run; ChatGPT answers on its own or says it can't help.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Denver this weekend?

negative.description: Medical diagnosis. Barbrabell plans training and gives no medical advice, so it shouldn't diagnose or call a tool; the expected answer suggests seeing a doctor or physical therapist, and may offer to plan around the pain once they have.
negative.prompt: My knee clicks when I bend it. Is it a torn meniscus?

negative.description: General writing with no training involved. None of Barbrabell's tools apply, so none should run; ChatGPT writes the poem itself.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about the ocean.

publication.release_notes: First release: coach your strength clients from ChatGPT. Roster review, programs and weekly plans from each client's own logs, bringing in existing programs, and client invites, with every change shown before it's saved.
